audit_notes: Model: same depletion model as used for tethered functional species: steady diffusion of mobile species with a volumetric source from clay dissolution, c(0)=0 at the wetted surface, c(1) = free mobile concentration at the reservoir front, surface loss flux J = S L/2 + D c_free/L. Design (no oil): S = 1e-12*50 = 5e-11 kg/(m^3 s), J = 5e-11*1.5e-4/2 = 3.75e-15 kg/(m^2 s) (0.1 mg/(m^2 yr)). Baseline: oil-containing conventional foul-release coating, no clay, 45 kg/m^3 free oil: J = 1e-15*45/1.5e-4 = 3e-10 kg/(m^2 s). Gain ~100 % by construction: the design has no mobile species, so this metric can hardly distinguish anything. Important caveats: (1) the realistic loss mechanism for platelets is wear of the silicone surface (a few um per year, i.e. ~0.1-0.3 g/(m^2 yr) of clay at 5 wt%), not dissolution; (2) the loss of material is not the loss of the anti-fouling function; natural clay and rock surfaces are colonised by biofilms, so whether a clay-faced surface resists slime at all is the open question and is not simulated; (3) against an oil-free silicone baseline the comparison is meaningless. Seawater chemistry: Na/Ca exchange collapses osmotic swelling; only 1-2 water layers remain (crystalline swelling), so the hydration layer is ~0.3-0.6 nm, thinner than on zwitterionic brushes. Dimensionless: S L^2/(D c_free) = 2.5e-5; platelet aspect ratio ~100-300. No structural concern at 5 wt% clay; the surface energy of the silicone rises where clay faces are exposed. Simulation coefficient: design loss flux 3.75e-15 kg/(m^2 s) (informational).
